title: Intro to the terminal
line: Move around, handle files and write your first shell script.

project.title: A script that tidies a messy folder
project.brief: Write tidy.sh on your own. Given a folder name, it makes text and images folders inside it, moves each .txt, .jpg and .png file into the right one and prints how many it moved.
checks: tidy.sh starts with a zsh shebang line and is executable
After a run no .txt, .jpg or .png file is left loose in the folder
It prints the number of files it moved

lessons.title: Find where you are
lessons.goal: Teach a complete beginner the macOS Terminal and zsh. Use pwd, ls and cd with tab completion to walk from the home folder to / and back, and show hidden files with ls -a.
lessons.passes: The last pwd prints the home folder, /Users/ and the user name.

lessons.title: Make folders and files
lessons.goal: Teach mkdir, mkdir -p and touch in the macOS Terminal by building a trail-log folder in the home folder with notes and photos folders inside and three empty day notes.
lessons.passes: trail-log holds notes and photos, and notes holds day1.txt, day2.txt and day3.txt.

lessons.title: Copy, move, rename and delete
lessons.goal: Teach cp, mv, rm and rm -r in the macOS Terminal, and that rm has no undo, by copying day1.txt to day1-backup.txt, renaming day3.txt to summit.txt and removing a scratch folder.
lessons.passes: notes holds day1-backup.txt and summit.txt, and day3.txt and scratch are gone.

lessons.title: Write lines into a file
lessons.goal: Teach echo with > and >> in the macOS Terminal, and how > overwrites while >> adds, by writing three lines about the weather and the trail into each of the three trail-log notes.
lessons.passes: day1.txt, day2.txt and summit.txt each hold three lines.

lessons.title: Read files with cat, less and head
lessons.goal: Teach reading text in the macOS Terminal with cat, less, head, tail and wc -l, and looking up a flag with man, by checking the three trail-log notes without opening an editor.
lessons.passes: wc -l prints a count of 3 for each of the three notes.

lessons.title: Match many files with wildcards
lessons.goal: Teach the * and ? wildcards in zsh by listing every .txt note in trail-log, copying day1.txt and day2.txt into a backup folder with one cp command and removing day1-backup.txt.
lessons.passes: backup holds day1.txt and day2.txt only, and day1-backup.txt is gone.

lessons.title: Pipes and grep
lessons.goal: Teach grep and the pipe in zsh by finding every line that mentions rain across the trail-log notes, sorting the matches, counting them with wc -l and saving the sorted lines to rain.txt.
lessons.passes: rain.txt holds every line from the notes that mentions rain, in sorted order.

lessons.title: Permissions and chmod
lessons.goal: Teach reading the rwx columns of ls -l and changing them with chmod in the macOS Terminal by making private.txt, a note that only its owner can read and write.
lessons.passes: private.txt has mode 600, read and write for the owner only.

lessons.title: Write a shell script
lessons.goal: Teach a first zsh script on macOS. Write newday.sh in nano with a shebang line for zsh, make it executable with chmod +x and have it create a note named with today's date.
lessons.passes: Running ./newday.sh makes a file in notes named with today's date.

lessons.title: Variables, arguments and a loop
lessons.goal: Teach shell variables, the $1 argument and a for loop in zsh by writing count.sh, which takes a word and prints how many lines mention it in each trail-log note.
lessons.passes: ./count.sh rain prints one line for each note with its count.
